transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-04-14 15:00 UTC | Duration: 47m | Attendees: Lydia Park, Marcus Nguyen (Redwood); Ravi Patel, Dana Morales, Elena K., Omar Ruiz (Summit)

Summary (auto): Align POC success criteria and telemetry to run two parallel benchmark configurations: Redwood hosted baseline and Dedicated reserved pool. Clarify dataset residency and encryption needs. Define timelines for pilot readiness.

[00:00] Lydia Park: hey everyone, thanks for joining on a tuesday afternoon, uh quick intros — i'm lydia from redwood, im the account exec, and with me is marcus our solutions engineer.
[00:18] Ravi Patel: hi all, ravi here, head of ml at summit analytics. we wanted to double check the pilot scope and what benchmarks you need.
[00:24] Marcus Nguyen: great, thanks. the goal for today is pretty pragmatic — agree success criteria, get exact workload numbers, and decide if we start pilot on hosted and then move to dedicated, or go straight to dedicated/private.
[00:36] Elena K.: quick context — our initial use case is automated insights for client dashboards. responses are short, usually 30-80 tokens, but we have some longer summarize flows to 250 tokens. average user session triggers 3 calls.
[00:51] Dana Morales: infra note — we have a soft egress budget and for some customers we must keep data in-eu if it's EU customer PII. also our security team will want SSO and audit logs.
[01:05] Lydia Park: perfect, those are important. can you give ballpark QPS?
[01:10] Ravi Patel: baseline 70 rps, peak bursts up to 350 rps during reports. daily active users about 120k, but most load is within 1 hour windows.
[01:22] Marcus Nguyen: thanks. so for the pilot we usually size for peak/2 and run a stress bench. we'll propose two configs: hosted baseline with autoscaling and dedicated reserved cluster sized for peak throughput with predictable latency.
[01:37] Omar Ruiz: sorry i'm late, joining now. small ask from security — is there a way to bring your control plane into our VPC or do you offer private deployment?
[01:47] Lydia Park: yep we support three modes — hosted api, dedicated reserved capacity (Redwood Dedicated) where customers get GPU pools, and private deployment (VPC or on-prem). each has tradeoffs on latency, cost predictability, and isolation.
[02:01] Dana Morales: cost predictability is huge. finance won't sign until we show committed spend vs variable hosted.
[02:08] Lydia Park: understood. decision criteria we usually see: data sensitivity/regulatory -> lean private; predictable throughput/cost -> dedicated; fast time-to-value -> hosted. but that rule-of-thumb can flip with latency and engineering constraints.
[02:21] Marcus Nguyen: for benchmarks, we need: 48h traces (or a sample), top 50 prompts, token length distribution, and target SLOs. also any retry/backoff behavior in your client.
[02:34] Ravi Patel: we can export traces. just to confirm — when you say benchmarks, do you run real-model runs or simulated latency?
[02:41] Marcus Nguyen: we'll run real runs against the model family you pick — we recommend starting with an open LLM variant we have in the catalog (we can mirror your closed model if needed for quality checks). we do token-level metrics, latency percentiles, and cost per 1k tokens.
[02:55] Elena K.: quality is critical too — we have a regression gate. if the model degrades more than 3% on our eval prompts we won't proceed.
[03:03] Lydia Park: noted — we'll hook Redwood Optimize evals and tie alerts to your eval set.
[03:09] Marcus Nguyen: a note about caching — prefix/k v cache can reduce cost for repeated prompts. our runtime supports KV-cache and prefix caching; please confirm how many distinct prompts you have vs templated ones.
[03:21] Ravi Patel: about 40% templated, rest are ad-hoc.
[03:25] Marcus Nguyen: that helps — caching can drop token spend and improve p95.
[03:30] Dana Morales: on the security front — KMS integration is required. we use AWS KMS. do you support customer-managed keys?
[03:37] Lydia Park: yes, both in Dedicated and Private you can bring your KMS. Hosted has envelope encryption but we can discuss key control via BYOK options in enterprise plans.
[03:47] Omar Ruiz: also SOC2 and ISO — do you have attestations?
[03:51] Lydia Park: we are SOC2 Type II and have ISO-27001, and we'll share our security pack. i'll attach the comliance binder after the call.
[03:59] Ravi Patel: timeline — we want a 4-week pilot. week 0 is instrumenting traces + agreement, weeks 1-2 benchmarks and tuning, week 3 is integration and canary, week 4 is eval and decision. reasonable?
[04:12] Marcus Nguyen: that's what we recommend. for a 4-week pilot we typically limit scope to a single model and a single route, so we can produce clear latency/cost numbers.
[04:23] Lydia Park: what success criteria should we sign to — propose: p95 latency < 200ms for standard prompts, cost per 1k tokens below your target (TBD), and quality regression < 3% on eval set.
[04:36] Elena K.: that works. add SLO for uptime 99.5% during pilot and readiness for VPC peering if needed.
[04:45] Marcus Nguyen: i will include pipeline for canary rollouts — if dedicated is chosen, we can do gradual rollout with fallback to hosted if capacity issues occur.
[04:55] Ravi Patel: can you give an example cost delta between hosted and dedicated? we need order-of-magnitude for procurement.
[05:01] Lydia Park: rough numbers — hosted variable costs might be 20-30% higher per token at high volume but no commit. Dedicated reserved can cut unit cost 40-55% depending on quantization and batching. Private adds infra overhead but gives full isolation. i'll send a cost banding table after this call.
[05:17] Dana Morales: network egress constraints — if we route to hosted, egress costs could be material. curious if Redwood can co-locate in our cloud region to avoid cross-region egress.
[05:26] Marcus Nguyen: yes; hosted endpoints can be regionally pinned. Dedicated can be provisioned in your VPC in some cases or via peering to avoid egress. private on-prem avoids that entirely.
[05:36] Elena K.: what about model versions and rollbacks? we need version pinning and canary.
[05:40] Marcus Nguyen: Redwood Console supports model pinning, canary rollouts, and automatic fallback policies. all config is part of the pilot config so you can validate rollbacks.
[05:49] Ravi Patel: for pilot inputs i'll share 48h traces and top 50 prompts. anything else?
[05:54] Marcus Nguyen: token distribution per prompt, concurrency distribution, and any latency budget from front-end to backend — are you measuring budget as front-to-back or just inference?
[06:03] Ravi Patel: front-to-back. our app budget is 300ms median, 500ms p95 for the full request. so inference needs to be below 200ms p95 to leave room for other services.
[06:14] Lydia Park: good to know. that gives us a clear engineering target.
[06:18] Elena K.: callouts — privacy: EU PII subset must not leave EU. for those cases we need dedicated or private in eu region.
[06:27] Marcus Nguyen: okay we can design routing rules: sensitive requests flagged and routed to a Private regional cluster, other traffic to hosted. this is common configuration.
[06:36] Dana Morales: any requirement for FIPS or HSM?
[06:39] Lydia Park: Dedicated and Private support HSM integrations for key storage; hosted has KMS envelope options. we'll share exact menus.
[06:46] Omar Ruiz: also compliance review: we'll need a brief architecture diagram for our audit team showing where logs live and access processes.
[06:52] Lydia Park: we'll attach architecture and an audit log sample.
[06:55] Marcus Nguyen: quick technical note — for benchmarks i'd like to run two modes: 1) hosted baseline with autoscale and typical batching, and 2) dedicated with reserved GPU pool and tuned batching/quantization profile. i'll run both against your prompt set and return latency and cost delta.
[07:10] Ravi Patel: do you need a license to run exact same model we use? we have a custom fine-tuned model.
[07:15] Marcus Nguyen: for fine-tuned models we can either accept a containerized model you provide for private pilot or use a functionally-equivalent open model for the hosted baseline to get perf characteristics. fine-tuned model runs will be part of the private/dedicated steps and may need a private deployment.
[07:29] Elena K.: ok, for pilot start let's use open variant for perf and later schedule a private run with our fine-tuned model.
[07:36] Lydia Park: agreed. i'll capture that in the SOW.
[07:39] Dana Morales: timeline items — who will sign SOW and legal review? procurement goes through me and procurement lead, legal will need the security binder.
[07:47] Lydia Park: Lydia (AE) will send draft SOW, redwood legal will provide the contract and security pack.
[07:53] Marcus Nguyen: on the bench outputs i'll include a runbook for how to tune batch sizes and the quantization options we tested.
[07:59] Ravi Patel: what's the expected pilot cost? we need a number to present to finance — rough estimate fine.
[08:05] Lydia Park: for a 4 week pilot, with hosted runs and a small dedicated reservation for a week of stress tests, expect order of magnitude $15k-30k depending on model size and total tokens. dedicated-only pilot would be higher up-front. i'll put ranges in the follow-up.
[08:19] Elena K.: can we also set a decision rubric — e.g., if cost saving > 30% and latency improvement > 20% choose dedicated; if not, choose hosted and revisit in 6 months.
[08:29] Marcus Nguyen: that's reasonable. i'll propose a simple scorecard in the pilot report.
[08:34] Lydia Park: any final questions?
[08:36] Omar Ruiz: one more — data retention. how long do you keep logs for hosted trial? we need logs purged after 30 days for this pilot.
[08:44] Lydia Park: we can set retention policy for the pilot to 30 days and provide deletion proof.
[08:48] Dana Morales: thanks. also include a note on SSO / SAML integration schedule.
[08:52] Lydia Park: noted.

[46:15] Lydia Park: quick recap and next steps — lydia to send pricing and SOW, marcus to run two benchmark configs once traces arrive, summit provides traces and prompts, dana confirms network and procurement path. target pilot kickoff week of 2026-04-27.
[46:35] Ravi Patel: sounds good, appreciate it.
[46:38] Marcus Nguyen: i'll add the canary and fallback steps to the report.
[46:41] Elena K.: thanks everyone.
[46:45] Lydia Park: thanks all, talk soon, bye.
